newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls Atlanta blasts "vile and malevolent".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls Atlanta blasts "vile and malevolent".

text.p: President Clinton issued a statement condemning two blasts at an Atlanta abortion clinic Thursday, calling them a "vile and malevolent act."

"The double bombing of a women's health clinic in Atlanta this morning was a vile and malevolent act," Clinton said in a statement read by White House spokesman Mike McCurry at the start of his daily briefing.

"Nobody has a right to use violence in America to advance their own convictions over the rights of others. We will get to the bottom of this. We will punish those responsible to the fullest extent that the law provides," the statement said.

"It is precisely because we take the constitutional rights and individual liberties of all of our people so seriously that I fought for and signed new legislation in 1994 to make it a federal crime to interfere with a woman exercising her constitutional right to visit a women's health centre."
McCurry said investigators from several federal agencies including the FBI were on the scene in Atlanta beginning the forensic probe of the blasts.

The first explosion shattered one side of the building housing the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre in a suburb known as Sandy Springs at around 9:30 a.m. EST. A clinic worker said at least four people were inside the facility at the time but no one was injured.
A little over an hour later a garbage container in the corner of an adjacent parking lot exploded, knocking people to the ground as federal and local officials sifted through nearby debris.
Police in Atlanta said there was no warning and they suspected bombs were responsible for both explosions.
McCurry said Clinton had seen footage of the blasts on television and had ordered his chief of staff Leon Panetta to get more information on them from the Justice Department.
